public_rationale: The cited study supports a narrower finding: arithmetic performance depends strongly on how frequent constituent terms are in training data. It does not establish the stated comparison between seen and unseen complete examples, or prove that no addition rule was learned. Treating those conclusions as equivalent would overstate the evidence.
limitations: The cited study evaluates GPT-J and GPT-Neo, not GPT-3 itself.
The earlier GPT-3 contamination check is informative context, not decisive evidence within the target period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Large language models do not learn an abstract notion of addition; they do markedly better on examples seen in training than on unseen ones.

statement.excerpt: Rather than inducing an abstract notion of addition (which is taken for granted in all modern microprocessor design) large language models learn addition piecemeal, performing markedly better on specific examples they have seen before than on examples they have not seen before.

our_interpretation: The surrounding text ties the observation to the arithmetic research reported earlier in 2022.
Seen versus unseen refers to pretraining exposure to particular addition examples, not merely the frequency of individual numbers.
An abstract notion of addition means a transferable addition rule; it need not imply perfect execution on every problem.
The target period is 2022 through the post date, following the explicit earlier-this-year context.
criteria.support_condition: Matched addition tests show a substantial advantage for examples present in pretraining, and controlled generalization tests support piecemeal learning rather than a transferable addition procedure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled tests show comparable performance on matched seen and unseen addition examples, or demonstrate a transferable addition procedure that cannot be explained by memorizing those examples.

evidence.explanation: The study finds addition accuracy associated with term and term-pair frequency in GPT-J and GPT-Neo. It compares more frequent with less frequent constituents, not matched complete equations known to be seen versus unseen; it also explicitly declines a causal interpretation.

The earlier report found 80.2% three-digit addition accuracy, while its search found matching expressions for only 17 of 2,000 addition problems. This cautions against assuming exact-example memorization, although the search covered limited expression formats and predates the target period.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A contemporaneous addition evaluation with verified complete-example exposure, matched difficulty, and tests distinguishing equation memorization from transfer of an addition procedure.
